Beginner Glossary

Plain-language definitions for the terms used throughout the workouts.

Quick guide
Working set

A set that counts toward the workout after the lighter warm-up sets are finished.

RPE

Effort from 1–10. RPE 8 means you could perform about two more clean reps.

RIR

“Reps in reserve”—the number of good repetitions you believe you had left.

Tempo

How quickly each part of a repetition is performed, especially the lowering phase.

Superset

Two exercises performed back-to-back before taking a full rest.

Drop set

Perform a hard set, reduce the weight, and immediately continue with more reps.

Finisher

A short final exercise intended to challenge the trained muscles or conditioning.

Deload

An easier training week that reduces fatigue while keeping the movement routine.

Client onboarding

Complete the coaching information in short sections. You can save and return without finishing everything at once.

0%Not started
0 of 9 onboarding sections ready
Complete the client sections, then a trainer records the baseline decision.
1 · Identity and contact

Confirm how the client should be identified and contacted. Changing this intake does not change the account login until a trainer reviews it.

2 · Goal contract and what success means

The training category helps program the workouts. The goal contract records what the client actually wants, why it matters, how progress will be measured, and what success means in their own words.

Make the goal measurable

Choose one main measure. This keeps the app honest: progress comes from real workout, attendance, or body-composition records when they exist—not a mystery score.

3 · Schedule, locations, and barriers

Usual training days and session length remain in the main client profile. Record the real-world factors most likely to affect consistency here.

4 · Equipment access

Select everything the client can reliably use. The trainer can narrow this further in the approved profile, and the filters apply to warm-ups, main work, conditioning, and cool-downs.

5 · Health readiness and current limitations

These questions support trainer review; they do not diagnose or clear anyone for exercise. A “yes,” current concerning symptom, clinician restriction, pregnancy/postpartum status, or unresolved pain must be reviewed before difficult training.

Report Pain or Discomfort

Choose what the symptom did to your movement. This report alerts your trainer and stays attached to the workout.

GreenNo pain. Continue as planned.
YellowMild awareness; movement stays normal. Modify if needed and monitor.
OrangeTechnique, range, or balance changes. Stop that exercise and substitute.
RedSevere, sharp, worsening, or concerning. End the workout and seek appropriate help.

This tool does not diagnose an injury. For emergency or serious symptoms, follow local emergency procedures.
